nodes.title: Validate quantities without blocking typing
nodes.why: The input keeps whatever the user typed, and only valid whole numbers reach the totals.
nodes.alternative: Clamp or rewrite the input value on every keystroke.
nodes.tradeoff: Rewriting fights the user mid-edit; a separate error line explains the problem instead.

nodes.title: Round transformers up
nodes.why: Three batteries need two transformers; rounding down would under-provision the site.
nodes.tradeoff: Rounding up matches the stated rule, and the tests check 3 and 4 batteries.

nodes.title: Sort a copy largest first
nodes.why: Placing big devices first leaves small gaps that later small devices can fill.
nodes.tradeoff: Input order is simpler but wastes space when sizes are mixed.

nodes.title: Put each device into the first row with room

anchor.snippet: const row = rows.find((candidate) => candidate.widthFt + device.widthFt <= maxWidthFt);

nodes.why: First-fit is easy to explain and never breaks the 100 ft limit.
nodes.alternative: Search every row for the tightest fit.
nodes.tradeoff: Best-fit can save a row in rare cases but is harder to reason about in a take-home.

nodes.title: Derive the whole site in one useMemo
nodes.why: Totals, rows and land size always come from the same quantities, so they cannot drift apart.
nodes.alternative: Keep totals and rows in state and update them in handlers.
nodes.tradeoff: Derived values need no synchronization; state copies need every handler to be right.

nodes.title: Compute the land from the packed rows
nodes.why: The land follows the real layout: the widest row times the number of rows times 10 ft.
nodes.alternative: Sum the device widths and divide by 100.
nodes.tradeoff: Division ignores the gaps the packing leaves; the rows are the truth.

nodes.title: Format money and energy for people
nodes.why: Floating sums such as 4.2 - 0.25 need rounding for display, and money needs thousands separators.
nodes.tradeoff: Raw floats leak values like 3.9500000000000006 into the UI.

nodes.title: Expose each row width as data
nodes.why: The 100 ft rule becomes visible to tests and to a reviewer reading the DOM.
nodes.tradeoff: CSS percentages are hard to assert; a data attribute is explicit.
